quizName: Hardest Questions in Maine Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you if:

options.text: You can touch your feet to the ground while sitting on it.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch your feet to the ground while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly if your feet can touch the ground while you sit on it. You should be able to reach and operate the controls easily.

questions.question: Which color is best for being seen on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green when riding. Bright clothing makes you easier to see at any time of day.

questions.question: When using an unfamiliar motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Test the seat to see if it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good condition.
Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
Ride normally because most bikes are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar bike, practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes. Learn the gear pattern before you start riding.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, clothing:

options.text: Should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Should not cover your arms or legs completely.
Should not include a jacket in warm weather.
Can protect you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect you if you crash.
questions.explanation: Good clothing protects you in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Your clothes should fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: The best source for information about your motorcycle is:
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It includes details about how your motorcycle works, how to operate it, and what maintenance it needs.

questions.question: Your body can only remove alcohol through:
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. There are no shortcuts to sobering up.

questions.question: What should you check before riding?

options.text: The wear and tread on your tires
How much cushion your seat has

questions.correctAnswerText: The wear and tread on your tires
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle. Inspect your tires, oil and fluid levels, lights, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: When it is obvious you are going to turn, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need a turn signal if pedestrians are nearby.
Only need a turn signal at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if it seems obvious. Other vehicles might be nearby that you cannot see. Signals are always necessary.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast:

options.text: Is okay if you stay under the speed limit.
Is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
Is okay if no other vehicles are nearby.
Can cause you to end up in another lane or off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to end up in another lane or off the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may lose control and drift into another lane or off the road. Always slow down before turning.

questions.question: A motorcycle has the best traction on:
questions.explanation: Many surfaces create poor traction for motorcycles. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal grates are all more hazardous than dry pavement.

questions.question: For best protection, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Only partially cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely for protection. Your clothing should fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials provide the best protection in an accident.

questions.question: Only ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time reduces alcohol in your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change your BAC.

questions.question: The best source of information for your motorcycle is:

options.text: Someone who has a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. The manual gives you specific information about your bike.

questions.question: For best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious defects.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Be equally as effective as a face shield.
Offer the same protection as a windshield.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only, not your face. A face shield protects your whole face and is better than goggles. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: If you can't avoid a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you can't avoid a slippery surface, slow down and keep your motorcycle upright.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Protective clothing includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves. A stocking cap is not considered protective gear.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road are slippery surfaces. Ride with extra caution on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: If wearing footwear with laces, the laces should:
questions.explanation: Tuck in your shoelaces securely so they don't catch on your motorcycle.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may pull out suddenly into your path.
Others may be driving slowly while looking for a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may pull out suddenly into your path.
questions.explanation: A driver might pull out of a parking space into your path without looking. Car doors may open into your lane and pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of having an accident?

options.text: Try to blend in with traffic so other drivers do not notice you.
Do not use turn signals unless you are riding at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your turn signals, brake lights, and lane position to show what you plan to do. Keep distance between you and other vehicles. Look 12 seconds ahead. Be ready to react if something dangerous happens.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear when riding?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. You should wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye or face protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: Which of these does not need to be checked regularly?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chain, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Even a small problem on a motorcycle can be very dangerous in traffic.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is fastened securely is the most important thing you can do to increase your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or high shoes that support your ankles give the best protection. Laced boots are best. High-top boots or heavy shoes work well too. If your shoes have long laces, tuck them away before riding.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider slow down?
questions.explanation: Riders often slow down by downshifting. Keep in mind that slowing down this way does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: What happens when you take a corner too fast?

options.text: You may drift into another lane.
It is better than going too slowly.
You will usually stay in your lane.
It is safe because motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drift into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to drift into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before you enter a turn or curve.

questions.question: How does riding with a passenger affect your motorcycle?

options.text: It usually makes no difference to how the motorcycle handles.
It is usually safe for riders who are just starting out.
It can change how the motorcycle handles.
It is recommended to help new riders get used to different situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can change how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: What should a rider constantly watch for while scanning the road ahead?

options.text: Places to escape to if needed.

questions.explanation: Scan the road ahead to watch for changes in traffic, dangerous road conditions, and escape routes. Be ready to react quickly to any changes.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
It keeps you in one spot in the lane and limits your movement.
It lets you depend on other drivers to find hazards.
It means you have to ride faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps ensure you have time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe motorcycle riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire to estimate the pressure.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare the height of the tire to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before every ride. A tire that looks okay may still be under-inflated, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Ask other friends to convince them not to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask other friends to convince them not to ride.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride a motorcycle. Do everything you can to stop them. Asking a group of friends to help convince them not to ride can be very effective.

questions.question: What clothing should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Clothing that covers your arms and legs completely.
Clothing that covers your arms completely but leaves your legs exposed.
Clothing that covers your legs completely but leaves your arms exposed.
Whatever clothing makes you most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing that covers your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely for proper protection.

questions.question: What reduces head and neck injuries?
questions.explanation: A high-quality helmet greatly reduces head and neck injuries. It is a rider's best protection in an accident.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the most protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection when riding.

questions.question: What should you do about mirror checks while riding?

options.text: Do them only on long trips.
Make them part of your regular scanning routine.
They don't help because you can't do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of normal riding. Also check them before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: Why should you wear riding gloves?

options.text: Do not wear them because they make your hands too hot.
They give you a better grip on the handlebars.
Do not wear them because they make it harder to use the controls.
Wear them only on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Wear gloves made of leather or another durable material. They improve your grip on the handlebars and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces have poor traction for motorcycles. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: What type of soles should motorcycle riding boots have?

options.text: Material that lets your feet breathe.

questions.explanation: Choose boots or shoes that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. The soles should be made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Do this even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: For the best protection, your helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly and have no visible damage.

questions.question: Which item does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: To stay safe, wear a DOT helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots that support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: If a friend has drunk too much and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Tell them to use empty roads.

questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has drunk too much to ride. Stop them by taking their keys if needed. Find them another way to get home.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Let other drivers share your lane.
Help you see others and be seen.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see and be seen. It should keep you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It should also discourage lane sharing and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: To get the most protection, choose a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. Your helmet should fit snugly all around.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet greatly lowers your chance of serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not limit your side vision.

questions.question: To improve your visibility, you can:
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright clothing with reflective materials. Use your headlight at all times. Use your signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: Which hand or foot controls the accelerator?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip and is controlled with your right hand.
